speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: extraordinary meeting of Huddersfield Council, meeting number 4485. I acknowledge the Wollongong people of the Eora nation, the traditional owners of the land in which we meet and the waters that surround. I pay my respects to their elders past, present and emerging. We thank you, Lord, for the honour of being called by our fellow citizens to this office of honour and trust. Give us grace, diligently and honourably, free from private interest or prejudice, to discharge the duties entrusted to us, to the common good and as in your sight, through Jesus Christ, our Lord, amen. Thank you. The first item on the agenda tonight is the election of the mayor. I'll hand over to, oh, my apologies. Obviously we have no apologies tonight. The other thing I'll call for is declarations of interest. I presume there won't be any. Thank you. I'll now, as I said before, the first item on the agenda is the election of the mayor. I'll pass over to Council's Legal and Governance Officer, Ms. Christina Parrs, who will be the returning officer for tonight's elections. Thank you, Mr. Chairperson. In accordance with the local government, general regulation 2005, I confirm that I have received more than one nomination for mayor of Hunterstown. I will now read out the names of the nominees and seek their confirmation that the nominee has accepted the nomination. Councillor Elizabeth Krasoy. Councillor Zach Miles.

speaker: zacmiles
text: I'll be withdrawing my nomination.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: And Councillor Ross Williams.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: I accept the nomination.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Thank you. As there is more than one candidate that's been nominated, the council must determine by resolution the method of voting for the position of mayor by way of one of the following, oh, sorry, Councillor Miles.

speaker: zacmiles
text: I move that we conduct the election by open voting.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Perfect. Do I have a seconder? Councillor Krasoy. All those in favour of resolution by way of open voting. That's passed unanimously. I'll pass back to you, Christina. Thank you. It's been resolved that the method of voting for the position of mayor will be done by a show of hands. Sorry, Councillor Miles.

speaker: zacmiles
text: Could I also ask that each of the candidates be given the opportunity to speak for five or 10 minutes on the reasons they're running for mayor and the experience that they're bringing to the role? I think.

speaker: bencollins
text: Second.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: I put it in the form of a motion. Can we put that motion to the council? Those in favour? Okay, that's passed. Is that unanimous? Councillor Williams, do you wish to vote on it? No. Councillor Williams, could you unmute? Yes, Mr. Deputy Mayor. Do you wish to vote no to that resolution?

speaker: rosswilliams
text: I'm not fussed at all. It's rather unusual. And it's not on the business paper. That's what we want to do.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Right, well, it's passed unanimously, I presume. Thank you. Each councillor is entitled to vote only once. I know, but what I might, so what I might do, do you want to actually, do you want to do the, actually, yeah, I can, sorry. I'll put that back. Apologies, councillors. If you're of a mind, now that the council's passed that motion in alphabetical order, if that is suitable, Mr. Chair, President? That's suitable. Yep, I might ask Councillor Cressoy if she would like to speak.

speaker: elizabethkrassoi
text: Sure, and thanks for the opportunity, Councillor Miles. I haven't prepared anything to say. It's not how we've done it in the past, but I'm honoured to have the opportunity on the record to say why I've put myself forward for the position of mayor on this occasion. I was elected as a truly independent councillor to Hunters Hill Council, having lived in the suburb for 18 years now. I believe that what I bring to the council table is a passion for my community and a determination to represent that community's needs to the council. And conversely, to represent the council's duties and jobs that we're doing to the community. As a resident, I wanted to see greater collaboration with the council and with our community groups in particular. As anyone who's followed me knows, I'm very passionate about our places, about placemaking people and how they connect and sustainability and how we as a council can support not only our own practice, but actually our community to do best practice in that area. Why me? As a 50 and a bit year old, I bring a lifetime of my own personal experience. My background is in sustainability. We have a couple of small businesses of our own. Having raised our children through the preschools and schools in the local area and navigating the streets and the footpaths and bringing my own understanding of the suburb to council, I guess. I feel that as a mayor, I would provide a moderate position on the council. We do have some sort of further to the right, some further to the left. I'm a true independent. I'm very much down the middle of the road. I feel that I respect and understand the relationship with the operational side of council. I try very hard as a councillor to walk that line of supporting our council operationally to deliver on the strategic planning that we as a council have overseen together and that we developed in consultation with our community. I sat today at a consultation actually down at Henley on the Henley Reserve, Gladesville Reserve Plans of Management. And I just felt really privileged to be there, not just because I've watched that area for so long, but just because I want to be part of the good decisions that are being made for my children in this suburb and for the children and grandchildren of future generations who come to this suburb. I'm guided by the hard work that women and councillors of all gender before us have done on our behalf to make our suburb the leafy and magnificent heritage suburb that it is. I'm guided by those children and grandchildren and the future that I hope they will navigate within our city. I'm guided by our city, our state and our country and our world and what goes on there and our place within it. And I'm guided by the general manager, her senior staff and the staff at council in every decision that I make. When we became councillors, we all did governance training. We all did councillor training. We've done meeting code of conduct training and governance training. And I believe that my experience chairing meetings will also come to that role as mayor. I am excited about how much I will need to learn in the role as mayor. And I will be looking to the expertise of my fellow councillors who have more experience than me and who have skills in other areas to me. Certainly when I became a councillor, I was excited that we all brought different skillsets to the table and I was looking forward to leaning into those skillsets and hoping we would work together well. I certainly hope that whether I'm your mayor or whether councillor Williams is your mayor, I certainly hope that this year politics can be put aside and that we can lean in together and deliver some of the great outcomes that we as a council have forged forward with over the last few years. Certainly since our new general manager, Lisa Miss Campbell has come on board. So that's why I put myself forward. I don't do it saying I have all the skills for the role. I do it with excitement, looking forward to learning the role and looking to the community and my fellow councillors and council staff to support me, to do the best work that I can for all of you internally. And as we look outward as well. Thanks for your time.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Thank you, Councillor Cressy. Councillor Williams.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: Thank you, Mr. Deputy Mayor. Yes, it's a great privilege to be able to serve your local community as a councillor. And it also is a great honour to have the opportunity to do that as the mayor of Hunters Hill. I bring to the table considerable experience in local government, but also in my professional career have worked extensively in state government and also in the private sector. I bring a wealth of understanding to how the government process works and how to get the best outcomes of those processes. My four years as a mayor, some considerable time ago now in 12, now what's coming up for 16 years on council gives me an enormous insight to the Hunters Hill community, to its needs, its desires, its expectations and more importantly, the values which it wishes us to uphold. It is a very important community, Hunters Hill. It's one that is unique in Sydney, if not Australia, in the way that it has great passion for both its environment, both built and natural. And it does look very strongly and demands its ability to act in local democracy. I think one of the reasons I came back to local government and on Hunters Hill Council after, I think it was about 17 years since I was on council previously, was that I fought many battles during that intervening period to support and ensure that Hunters Hill is here for us all today. Most recently, the merger process between Hunters Hill, Lane Cove and Ride, which was one that the community rose to that occasion as it has in the past, whether it's aircraft noise, whether it's schools, whatever. The Hunters Hill community always wants a strong voice and I'm hoping to be able to help communicate that voice through council decision-making. We've just had a very important term of council. We've been through the process of transition, enormous transition and many people in our community are not aware of the enormous changes that have occurred under the leadership of our new general manager. Those changes will put Hunters Hill in a very good place into the future, both from an administrative point of view, from transparency point of view, from our responsiveness to the community's needs. Those systems are now in place or if not in the final stages of being put in place. So over the next year, couple of years, I think the community will see major improvements in the outcomes that council delivers for it and on behalf of it. Moving into the future, the rewards we'll get from that will be great and will help us sustain ourselves. But there are other issues and other decisions which council has to make over the next 12 months, which I think will become quite pivotal in the future of Hunters Hill. And like with our administrative changes and the systems that underpin that, there's great innovation and great desire to do things in a way that gets the best outcome for our community. So I'd be hoping to provide that strong leadership, which I've demonstrated over many years, both in my professional career, my community work, as well as previous roles on council. I'd like to offer to the other councillors a warm opportunity to engage and be part of the process and to make sure that all voices are heard. We all come with different points of view and that point of view needs to be put and the decision of council respected. And I think we've been able to achieve outcomes over the last three years together. And as we move into this next phase of completing the transition from the ministry point of view and looking to our sustainability, both financially and from our contribution to the environment we live in, as well as the opportunities, which I think that our organisation and our community have available to them over the next 12 months. So I look forward to the opportunity and I see it as a great honour. And I now put myself in the hands of the councillors and I wish councillor Crassely good luck.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Thank you, councillor Williams. I'll pass back to the attorney, and obviously to you, Dr. Mallard. In accordance with the RLG requirements, we need to determine the order for the tally sheet. I'll now write each, I have each candidate's name on a slip of paper and I'll deposit it into this barrel. The first name out of the barrel will be written first on the tally sheet. And then the second name will be written second and we'll vote in that order.

speaker: zacmiles
text: This is a show of hands, we don't need a tally sheet.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Say again?

speaker: bencollins
text: Yeah, we can just show of hands. No.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: It's about the order of the voting. So whoever's name gets pulled out first, we vote on that councillor first. Of course. We vote on that councillor. So I'm popping in Elizabeth Crassely, councillor Elizabeth Crassely. I'm showing that the barrel is empty. Yes. Now we have councillor Ross Williams. First on the tally list is councillor Elizabeth Crassely. Second on the tally list is councillor Ross Williams. Each councillor is entitled to vote only for one candidate. And if a councillor does not vote, I'll clarify and confirm with that councillor that they are abstaining. And that's an informal vote. Now, would those councillors voting for councillor Crassely, please raise your hand. Thank you. That's two votes. That's councillor Crassely and councillor McLaughlin. And with those councillors voting for councillor Williams, please raise your hand. Thank you. That's four votes. We've got the deputy mayor, Jim Sanderson, councillor Zach Miles, councillor Ben Collins, and now mayor Ross Williams. Congratulations. I declare that councillor Ross Williams is elected as mayor of Hunters Hill until the local government election scheduled for September, 2021 takes place. Congratulations, Mayor Williams.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: Thank you very much. And thank you councillors for your support. And I look forward to working closely with you over the next 12 months.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Thank you. Now, the second order of business on the business paper is for the election of the deputy mayor. And again, in accordance with the local government regulations, I confirm that we have received more than one nomination for the deputy mayor. Yes, councillor Crassely.

speaker: elizabethkrassoi
text: I would like to withdraw my nomination. Thank you.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Thank you. And I'll just confirm with the other nominees that they accept their nomination. So we have councillor Ben Collins. Yes. Thank you. And councillor Jim Sanderson. I'll accept the nomination. Thank you. So as more than one candidate has been nominated, the council again must determine by resolution the method of voting for this position of deputy mayor by one of the following methods. That's the open voting, ordinary ballot or preferential ballot. And councillor Crassely, you'd like to put the motion?

speaker: elizabethkrassoi
text: That we vote for open voting. Thank you. Excuse me.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Yes, councillor Collins.

speaker: bencollins
text: I'd actually like to withdraw my nomination. I thought we did that after. So councillor Sanderson is due to leave.

speaker: clrjimsanderson
text: Okay. Then, thank you. And as there is no, we only have one nomination for deputy mayor. Congratulations, councillor, deputy mayor Sanderson. And we confirm that you're our deputy mayor for 104 until the next election. Thank you very much for that privilege to act as deputy mayor for another four months. I look forward to serving this community as I always have. Thank you. And we'll move on to the next item on the agenda, which is the, which in actual fact will be a meeting that will now be conducted by councillor Williams as the elected mayor.

speaker: rosswilliams
text: Thank you, councillor Sanderson. And congratulations on being returned as deputy mayor of Hunter's Hill. We now move on to the second matter for tonight. And that is item 2.1, which is the delegation of powers to both the mayor and the deputy mayor. So there's a paper before you and a recommendation. Is there a mover for the recommendation? Councillor Cressoy, councillor McLachlan is a seconder. Is there any discussion? If not, I'll put the motion. All those in favour? Against? Declare it carried. As I've had the opportunity to talk about what I see as being important in my role over the next 12 months, I won't go any further into that, but I would like to just make a quick comment in relation to our outgoing mayor, councillor Bennett or now Mr. Bennett. I can't add much more than what was in the local paper today, but I'd like to acknowledge his contribution to Hunter's Hill over the last eight years. And in particular, the last three years as mayor. And during his first term, he was very much involved in the campaign or the process of protecting Hunter's Hill against the merger. But also he was very keen and passionate about the finances of council and did achieve a lot in that time. And we move into the current term where he has led council, as I indicated before that council has been through a major transition over the last two years in particular with our new general manager and under the leadership and steady hand of councillor, Mr. Bennett, it was a smooth transition. And as I say, we will get great benefit out of that process. So I thank councillor Bennett for his contribution or former mayor councillor Bennett and the community is grateful for what you've done. And some of that will become very evident as we move forward over the remainder of this term and into the next term of council. So I look forward to working closely with all you and I also look forward to working closely with the general manager and the staff and making sure that we fulfil our obligations to the community and also fulfil some of the opportunities that are now available for us as we move forward. So I don't believe there's any further business for tonight's meeting. It was an extraordinary meeting. And so therefore there's only the business that was on the paper that we deal with. So with that, I look forward to our first meeting together in a week's time and I close the meeting. Thank you.

speaker: bencollins
text: Thank you.
